title: User profile errors
executive_summary: INC-006 (SEV2, user profile errors) is INCONCLUSIVE. The root cause could not be established. user-service error rate rose from about 0.4% to about 23% (max 33.5%) starting 2026-09-17T21:03Z (met-user-service-error_rate-2055-2130). Logs show 19 ERRORs of 'Connection to postgres-primary:5432 refused' (logpat-user-service-f82ed4bd) and 9 'connection reset by peer' errors against postgres-primary:5432 (logpat-user-service-97a18e1d), first at 21:03:00Z and 21:03:08Z. The only node-tagged signal is a single nf_conntrack 'table full' WARN on usr-node-3 at 21:02:00Z (logpat-user-service-227e81bb), which does not repeat and is not linked to the errors by node. No deployments were recorded for any service 18:00-21:30Z. Three hypotheses remain unresolved: H1 (network-path failure, confidence 0.20, needs evidence), H3 (unrecorded change on the path, confidence 0.08, needs evidence), and H2 (postgres-side degradation, rejected). No hypothesis is adequately supported.

critic_review.summary: No hypothesis is adequately supported. Verified evidence: user-service error_rate steps from ~0.4% to ~23% at 21:03Z. DB errors are 'refused' (19 pattern hits) and 'connection reset by peer' (9), first at 21:03:00Z and 21:03:08Z. The only node-tagged signal is a single nf_conntrack 'table full' WARN on usr-node-3 at 21:02:00Z. Re-querying user-service logs confirmed the 21:03-21:09 error burst and that the WARN has no repeats. No deployments were recorded for any service 18:00-21:30Z. Config-change and postgres metric data for 21:00-21:30Z are missing or empty. H1 is plausible in timing, but the one-off WARN cannot sustain 25 minutes of failure, it is not linked to the errors by node, and conntrack drops normally produce timeouts rather than 'refused' signatures. H2 is weakened by onset timing: rollups at 20:50 and 20:58 completed without user-service errors, and postgres shows routine checkpoints with no FATAL or connection-limit messages. Its post-onset server state is unknown because postgres metrics are missing. H3 is an unrecorded change with no positive evidence. Round 3 is the final round, so the remaining gaps cannot be closed by further requests within this investigation.

assessments.reasoning: Timing fits (conntrack WARN 21:02Z precedes first DB error 21:03Z), but the evidence is thin: a single WARN with no drop counters, no per-node split of errors, and a 'refused' error signature that does not match silent conntrack drops. Node concentration is unverified, so usr-node-3 is not confirmed as the culprit.

Onset does not track the rollups. Earlier rollups at 20:50 and 20:58 completed with no user-service errors until 21:03. Postgres logs show routine checkpoints and no FATAL, restart, or connection-limit messages after onset. Postgres metrics for 21:00-21:30Z are missing, so this is not a positive exclusion, but nothing supports the claimed mechanism. The rollup-to-refused-connection link is temporal correlation only.

Unrecorded change is possible but has no positive evidence. Deployments are empty and the config feed is empty for 18:00-21:11Z. The reset-by-peer signal is weak and not specific to a middlebox. Cannot be accepted without network, LB, or DNS records, which are not obtainable with the available tools.

unsupported_assumptions: That the single conntrack WARN on usr-node-3 causes 25 minutes of failure across the service, since no drop counters or repeated events were shown
That the 'refused' errors come from the network path rather than from postgres, since no connection-acceptance logs or postgres metrics cover the failure window
That the rollups cause the failures, given that earlier rollups completed without errors
That the flat db_conn_util on user-service rules out pool-side causes, since metrics are not split by node
alternative_explanations: Network-path or middlebox fault on the user-service to postgres-primary path (H1 or H3), with the node-level conntrack exhaustion on usr-node-3 as one possible trigger
Intermittent postgres-side connection refusal or reset during the post-onset window, for which postgres metrics are missing and cannot be confirmed as healthy (H2 in a weaker form)
Subset of user-service nodes or client-side connection handling failing, with error lines lacking a host tag so the split by node cannot be done

corrective_actions: Mitigate the user-service failure now: check whether the errors are confined to particular nodes (usr-node-3 first), and drain or restart affected user-service instances to clear any stale or exhausted connections.
Verify end-to-end connectivity from user-service hosts to postgres-primary:5432 (TCP connect, DNS resolution, endpoint/IP), and check for any firewall, proxy, or load-balancer changes on that path.

On usr-node-3, inspect conntrack utilization and drop counters (nf_conntrack_count vs nf_conntrack_max, drop statistics) to test H1 directly, since the single WARN alone does not explain 25 minutes of failure.

Check postgres-primary connection acceptance and health directly (max_connections, FATAL messages, listener status, pg_stat_activity) for 21:00-21:30Z, because postgres metrics for this window are missing.
preventive_actions: Add per-node tagging to user-service database error logs so failures can be split by host.
Record configuration, network, and credential or certificate changes in the change feed, including intermediate proxies, firewalls, and load balancers, so unrecorded changes can be ruled in or out.
Set conntrack capacity alerts and tune nf_conntrack_max and timeouts on user-service nodes to prevent table exhaustion.
Ensure the metrics pipeline covers postgres-primary and per-node user-service metrics, and fix the query limits and service naming that caused the failed queries in this investigation.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on user-service error_rate above 2% for 3 consecutive minutes, and on the count of 'refused' and 'connection reset by peer' errors to postgres-primary:5432 per node.
Monitor nf_conntrack usage and drop counters per node on user-service hosts, with alerts above 80% utilization or any sustained drops.

Collect postgres-primary connection metrics (active and total connections, refused connections, FATAL events, checkpoint and lock activity) at 1-minute resolution, and alert on any gap in these metrics.
Track TCP connect latency and failure rate from user-service to postgres-primary:5432 with synthetic probes from each node.
limitations: The root cause could not be established; the status is INCONCLUSIVE.
The single conntrack WARN on usr-node-3 (21:02Z) does not repeat and cannot by itself explain roughly 25 minutes of failure. No drop counters were available.
Postgres metrics for 21:00-21:30Z are missing or empty, so postgres-side health after onset cannot be confirmed.
user-service error lines lack a host tag, so the error distribution across nodes is unknown.
Configuration-change data for 21:00-21:30Z is missing or empty; no deployments were recorded.
Metric queries failed for user-service (too many metrics requested) and for usr-node-3 (not a known service), so some signals were not collected.

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.

conclusion: Root cause could not be conclusively established with the available evidence. The root cause of INC-006 is not established.
